podcast.title: Anonymous Email Promotion
podcast.body: Two days after the initial website announcement, an anonymous email was sent to individuals managing fan websites of Radiohead (part of "Group W," official fan web group). This email provided more detailed information about Thom Yorke's solo album, including its political themes, its origins from discarded `Kid A` sessions, and the use of the King Canute motif for the album cover. "dos días más tarde se publicaba un extraño y mey la nónimo a los que las personas que gestionaban algunas de las web que fueron parte del grupo West [...] les llevó un mail medio anónimo en el cual se hidraba más infamacian sobre el disco en solita de tom Jor."

podcast.title: Anti-Spotify Stance
podcast.body: Thom Yorke has maintained a strong rejection of Spotify and similar platforms since their inception, primarily due to disagreements over how royalties are distributed and how artists are compensated. He views the payment system as insufficient. "Tom Jork es una persona que siempre ha tenido un grandísimo rechazo de Spotify a muchas de estas plataformas, por como se reparten los derechos de los royales, y si como se pagan dinero, o según sus palabras como no, se pagan dinero por estas cosas"

podcast.title: Atoms for Peace Album Artwork by Stan Lee Donwood
podcast.body: Thom Yorke's involvement with Atoms for Peace included Stan Lee Donwood designing the graphic work for the band's album, continuing their collaborative artistic relationship. "el álbum de Atoms for Peace, él diseñó también el famoso logo de losso."

podcast.title: Atoms for Peace Music Absence
podcast.body: Music from Thom Yorke's band, Atoms for Peace, is not available on Spotify. Along with his solo album "The Eraser," there are no indications that this material will ever be made available on the platform, signifying his continued resistance. "con la banda que se inventó de Atons For Peace, no los tenemos en Spotify, no tiene pinta de que los vendíamos a tener en Spotify nunca."

podcast.title: Bear Logo Acceptance and Evolution
podcast.body: Tom Yorke confirmed in an interview that he initially admired the macabre image of the bear and used it exclusively for "Kid A" (QD) advertising. The bear's widespread acceptance by the public ultimately led to its adoption as one of Radiohead's standard logos, despite not being initially conceived as such. "Tom Yorke hacía referencia de que le había gustado un montón, esa imagen macabra de losos que la usó solo como publicidad para el QD. Pero luego le acabó gustando un montón, tuvo un montón de aceptación y que finalmente se quedó como uno de los logán se está en der de la banda."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Birth and Origin
podcast.body: Born on October 7, 1968, in the small English town of Wellingboro. "He's from a tiny English town called Wellingboro. His birthday was October 7, 1968."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Burial's Influence on Rhythmic Approach
podcast.body: Thom Yorke became a dedicated follower of Burial after 2006 and reinterpreted his own method of working with music, particularly focusing on rhythmic bases inspired by Burial's style. He has publicly stated that his album "The King of Limbs" and his solo career, including "Tomorrow's Modern Boxes," are directly influenced by Burial's rhythmic innovations. "Tom York después el 2006 se convierte con auténtico seguidor de burial y reinterpreta casi su manera de trabajar la música a partir de las bases ritmias de burial haría un disco prácticamente inspirado en las bases ritmias de burial que es el King of Limbs."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Childhood Nickname
podcast.body: Due to his pale and thin appearance at school, Tom was given the nickname "Salamander." This led to him getting into "a lot of fights," which even boxing lessons from his father couldn't significantly help. "he picked up the nickname Salamander."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Co-Designed Corrais Mobile Application
podcast.body: Thom Yorke, along with Stan Lee Donwood, co-designed a mobile application known as "los hechos a Corrais," which integrated image, sound, and an "astral journey" experience, acclaimed as an "authentic work of art." "llegaron incluso juntos a diseñar una aplicación de móvil que mezclaba imagen, sonido y una especie de viaje astral, los hechos a Corrais, la famosa aplicación que hicieron juntos que fue un auténtico obra de arte."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Stanley Donwood - El artista tras las portadas de Radiohead

podcast.title: College Plans and Early Jobs
podcast.body: Before attending university, Tom decided to take a year off. During this time, he worked selling men's suits, a job he "hated." He then found a "better job" working in a mental hospital before eventually enrolling at Oxford. "Tom decided to take a year off before university. He spent some time selling men's suits, something that he hated. So he got a better job. It gave him a mental hospital before he went back and enrolled in Oxford."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Criticism of Streaming Services
podcast.body: Tom York is cited as one of the artists who "rage against the rise of streaming music services," indicating his strong opposition to this modern model of music distribution. "For example, guys like Tom York and David Byrne rage against the rise of streaming music services."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cyclical Creative Process
podcast.body: Tom Yorke is characterized by a distinctive creative pattern, marked by alternating phases of intense creative explosion and profound creative crisis or depression. The "Kid A" sessions, for example, represent the zenith of his creative output during such an explosive phase. "Tom George es una persona que combina enormes fases de explosión creativa con enormes fases de crisis creativa y de depresión."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: OK Computer vs  Kid A: ¿Qué disco fue más importante?

podcast.title: DJ Gig at Campus Pub
podcast.body: To supplement his income, Tom worked as a DJ at a campus pub. He was quite skilled and his regular Friday night gigs often attracted "a thousand people or more" to hear him spin. "Tom supplemented his income working as a DJ at a campus pub. And he was pretty good too."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dr. Shock Alias
podcast.body: Tom Yorke used the pseudonym Dr. Shock for artistic expression projects that were not musical in nature. Under this alias, he signed various paintings and collaborated with Stanley Donwood on visual arts, including projections and the comic that inspired the Radiohead bear logo. "Dr. Shock realmente es el seudónimo con el que Tom York hacía ciertos trabajos de expresión artística que no era musical. Es el nombre como el que firmó algunos cuadros, incluso trabajos con Stan Lee Donwood sobre artes, sobre proyectiones y estas cosas."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Early Musical Frustration
podcast.body: Tom received his first guitar at the age of eight. However, he quickly became so frustrated with the instrument that he "smashed the thing to pieces in a big temper tantrum." "He got his first guitar at age eight, but he soon got so frustrated with it that he smashed the thing to pieces in a big temper tantrum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Band
podcast.body: After overcoming his initial frustration with the guitar, Tom formed his first band at age 10. "he eventually got his act together, and a few years later he formed his first band. This was age 10."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Guitar Hero
podcast.body: Tom York's earliest guitar hero was Brian May of Queen, whose guitar solo in "Bohemian Rhapsody" he still admires. "And his first guitar hero, it was Brian May of Queen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Impact on Radiohead's Label Transition
podcast.body: Thom Yorke's solo album, `The Eraser`, played a crucial role in Radiohead's ability to transition from EMI Records to XL Recordings. It effectively served as the first material to demonstrate their new creative freedom under the independent label, paving the way for the band's subsequent releases. "este disco aunque es el tom Jorney solitario llegó muchísimo a sentar el grupo primero porque le permitió moverse a X se le recorde ese primer material de rey de oje que hace la transición de mía a X se le recorden."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Incorporation of Hip Hop
podcast.body: Thom Yorke is noted as an artist who has been incredibly focused on incorporating influences from modern hip hop music into his sound, lyrics, and overall communication style within rock music. "tenemos incluso casos como el de Tom Yor de Radiohead o que incluso Bjork que hace tiempo que están increíblemente centrados en incorporar influencias de la música hip hop moderna al sonido pero sobre todo a las letras y a la manera de comunicar que tenemos en el rock moderno."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Influenced by Jeff Buckley
podcast.body: Thom Yorke is explicitly mentioned as one of the major singers who was significantly influenced by Jeff Buckley's unique singing style and intimate approach to music. He frequently references Jeff Buckley, indicating a deep artistic connection and impact. "tan yor que hace referencia a Jeff Buckley como muy a menudo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Interest in Electronic Music and Technology
podcast.body: Tom Yorke developed a keen interest in electronics, exploring various new music systems. He learned from other electronic artists and became proficient in using sampling machines and recording canned sounds. These new interests and acquired skills became fundamental to the future direction and sound of Radiohead. "Él se ha interesado mucho por la electrónica, conocía muchos otras artistas electrónicos que le habían enseñado muchos sistemas de música nuevos, él aprendió a utilizar muchísimas máquinas desampleados, agravar sonidos en latados."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Involvement in Radiohead Website
podcast.body: Yorke was heavily involved in Radiohead's official website, indicating his broader engagement beyond just musical creation. "Oh, and did I mention his heavy involvement in Radiohead's official website?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: King Canute Allegory for Tony Blair
podcast.body: Thom Yorke used the medieval figure of King Canute the Great on the cover of his 2006 solo album `The Eraser` as a direct comparison to Tony Blair. This allegory was intended to critique Blair's perceived "grandiosity" and "superiority" in the world, particularly in the context of the UK's involvement in "Iraqgate" and the failure of international climate change summits. "decidió usar al rey canuto el grande [...] para un poco usar la cometa fras sobre Tony Blair y el papel que está teniendo Tony Blair de grande osigacia y de un poco de su prioridad hacia el mundo que tiene y que está rastrando a su país a todos estos conflictos."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Later Loss of Interest in Exit Music (For a Film)
podcast.body: With the passage of time, Thom Yorke significantly lost interest in *Exit Music (For a Film)*. This diminished interest was the reason he permitted the song to be used in numerous soundtracks for various television series and films many years after its initial release. "Curiously, Thom Yorke has lost a lot of interest in it over the years and in the end he has allowed it to appear in many soundtracks of many television series and films years later because he has lost quite a bit of interest in it."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Meeting Stanley Donwood
podcast.body: While performing with The Headless Chickens in Exeter, Tom York met Stanley Donwood. Donwood went on to become, and remains, Radiohead's primary artist responsible for all their artwork and promotional materials. "it was while at Exeter, and playing in this band, that Tom met Stanley Donwood. He would go on to become a radio head's key guy when it came to artwork and promotional material."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: NME Interview on Kid A Material
podcast.body: In an interview with NME, Tom Yorke expressed the overwhelming volume of material generated during the "Kid A" sessions. He famously stated that he wished he could have released ten albums from the content produced during that period, indicating the difficulty he faced in selecting what to include. "En una entrevista a enemy Tom George llegó a decir que le hubiese gustado sacar 10 agúmes puntos con esa gollquidad porque realmente llevo un punto en que él no sabía que renunciar."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Personal Friend of Stan Lee Donwood
podcast.body: Thom Yorke is a personal friend of Stan Lee Donwood, a fact that was eventually confirmed, dispelling long-standing rumors about Donwood's true identity. "es un amigo personal de Thom Yorke."

podcast.title: Physical Characteristics and Health
podcast.body: Described as a "delicate little guy," standing approximately 5'5". He was often "sickly and skinny," which was a source of worry for his father, a chemical engineer and championship boxer. Tom was born with a partially paralyzed left eye, with the eyelid fixed in a downward position. After several surgeries intended to correct it, the fifth operation resulted in his distinctive "droopy eye" and reduced vision of about 50% on that side. He wore an eye patch during his first couple of years in school. "Tom is a delicate little guy, standing about 5'5"."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Political Frustration and Global Events
podcast.body: Thom Yorke was profoundly affected by global events, specifically the United Kingdom's role in "Iraqgate" and the perceived failures of two major climate change summits, which he described as "authentic disasters." This frustration stemmed from the first world's passivity regarding climate change and his own country's involvement in conflict. "Tom Jor sienta una enorme frustración interior hacia la pasividad del primer mundo por el cambio climático y sobre todo por el papel que está teniendo su país el reino unido en la guerra de radeigate."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Post-Trilogy Creative Crisis
podcast.body: Following Radiohead's intense recording period for `Kid A`, `Amnesiac`, and `Hail to the Thief`, Thom Yorke entered a significant creative crisis, finding himself unable to work on new material. During this time, he continuously listened to discarded recordings from the `Kid A` and `Amnesiac` sessions at home, marveling at their quality. "el esté en verso una enorme crisis creativa en la que es incapaz de trabajar en material nuevo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Pre-Kid A Creative Explosion Assessment
podcast.body: Tom Yorke characterized the period immediately preceding the release of "Kid A" as the band's most significant explosion of artistic creativity. During this time, the band produced a wealth of music alongside numerous other projects, such as posters, short films, videos, animations, and comics. "la mayor explosión de creatividad artística de la banda, como siempre ha referido a Tom York a ese periodo del que no solo salió muchísima música sino que salieron un montón de otros proyectos."

podcast.title: Restlessness and Work Ethic
podcast.body: Yorke is described as a workaholic who constantly needs to make music. When Radiohead took time between albums after their record deal ended, he used this period to work on his solo material. "He's one of those guys who always has to keep making music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rumored to be Stan Lee Donwood
podcast.body: For many years, there was a widespread and plausible rumor that Thom Yorke himself was operating under the pseudonym of Stan Lee Donwood, responsible for all of Radiohead's graphic work, due to Donwood's extreme reclusiveness. "durante muchos años había el grandísimo rumor y con mucho sentido de que era el propio Thom Yorke que actúa con el Seidónimo de Stan Lee Donwood, el que hacía todo el trabajo gráfico del grupo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Satisfaction and Refusal for Romeo + Juliet
podcast.body: After composing *Exit Music (For a Film)* for the *Romeo + Juliet* film commission, Thom Yorke found himself immensely satisfied with the song's tragic and "pompous" outcome. His profound satisfaction was such that, ironically, he ultimately refused to allow the song to be included in the film's final credits, despite having been specifically commissioned for that purpose. "The song is so tragic and pompous that Thom Yorke was very satisfied with the result and the problem is that he was so satisfied with the result that in the end he refused to include it in the film."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Radiohead - Exit Music For a film tiene una historia un tanto curiosa

podcast.body: Stan Lee Donwood created all the graphic work for Thom Yorke's solo projects, referred to as "A.R.I.C.E.," further cementing their artistic partnership beyond Radiohead. "ha hecho también todo el trabajo gráfico de los trabajos en solitario que ha hecho Thom Yorke, tanto de A.R.I.C.E."

podcast.title: Stage Fright and Writer's Block
podcast.body: As a member of Radiohead, Yorke faced significant obligations and pressures which occasionally led to paralyzing cases of stage fright and writer's block. "As a member of Radiohead, he had a lot of different obligations and pressures, some of which resulted in occasionally paralyzing cases of stage fright and writer's block."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Surprise Solo Album Announcement
podcast.body: The release of Thom Yorke's solo album was entirely unexpected by the public. Information about the album was initially published discreetly as a tiny announcement in a "dead spot" on Radiohead's `Hail to the Thief` website, specifically the "theeraser" section, which was known for answering random questions. "en uno de los puntos muertos que tenía la web que se llamaba de irayser hizo una pequeñísima publicación anunciando que sacaría un nuevo disco y al todo el mundo le pilló fuera del juego."

podcast.title: Twilight Soundtracks Contribution
podcast.body: Thom Yorke contributed to the various *Twilight* soundtracks that accompanied the film series. These soundtracks featured a nice selection of tunes, mostly album cuts and outtakes, from a range of artists spanning different genres. "The Paramore, Lincoln Park, Collective Soul, Death Cab for Cutie, Tom York, the Killers, Editors, Metric, Block Keys, Dead Weather, Beck, Vampire Weekend, Florence in the Machine."

xref.title: Glastonbury 1997 Performance Issues
xref.body: Radiohead's set at Glastonbury Festival on June 28, 1997, considered by some to be the "best show of all time," was initially fraught with technical difficulties. Halfway through their set, the band couldn't hear their stage monitors, leading to missed cues and frustration, almost causing them to walk off stage. To exacerbate matters, a roadie's spotlight kept blinding Thom Yorke. Yorke requested the lighting be turned onto the crowd, which coincided with the monitor problems clearing up and the "magic" setting in, solidifying their legend. "The group couldn't hear their stage monitors, and everyone started missing their cues. Frustration set in, and it looked for a while that Radiohead was going to cut things short and just walk off stage."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Thom Yorke's Personal Tragedy (2016)
xref.body: Thom Yorke and his partner, Rachel, separated after 16 years. A few months after the release of "A Moon-Shaped Pool" in December 2016, Rachel tragically died of cancer. "Another sad thing, Tom York and his partner Rachel separated after 16 years, and then she died of cancer that December, a few months after the album came out."

xref.title: Return to Toronto and Memorial (July 19, 2018)
xref.body: Radiohead did not perform in Toronto again until July 19, 2018, six years after the fatal stage collapse. During this concert, with the legal case still stalled, Thom Yorke publicly addressed the situation from the stage, and the band observed a moment of silence for Scott Johnson before continuing their performance. "Radiohead didn't play Toronto again until July 19, 2018."

xref.title: Frustration with Music Leaks
xref.body: Radiohead was deeply annoyed by the pervasive issue of music leaks, especially in the internet era, where a single file from a hard drive could undermine meticulously planned marketing campaigns and result in significant lost revenue. Their last four albums, plus Thom Yorke's solo record, had all leaked prematurely, sometimes months in advance, prompting the band to consider a radical business model to prevent such occurrences. "In fact, the last four Radiohead albums, plus Tom York's solo record somehow made it into the wild before they were supposed to, sometimes weeks before, and sometimes months before, which really ticked them off."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Overcoming Technical Difficulties at Glastonbury
xref.body: During their Glastonbury Festival set on June 28, 1997, Radiohead encountered major technical problems, including stage monitor malfunctions and a roadie continually shining a spotlight directly into Thom Yorke's eyes. The turning point occurred when Yorke yelled for the light to be turned on the crowd, which seemingly cleared the monitor issues and unleashed a "magic" atmosphere, leading many to regard this gig as historically significant. "All these people in a field in the dark suddenly lit up and the monitor problems cleared up and that was the moment the magic set in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Record Deal Free Agency
xref.body: After their record deal ended, Radiohead became free agents and decided to take their time exploring the market before committing to another label. This period of inactivity for the band prompted Thom Yorke to pursue his solo work. "But when the band ended up at the end of their record deal, they became free agents."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Thom Yorke's Writer's Block and Computer Vocals
xref.body: During the creation of *OK Computer*, Thom Yorke experienced a severe case of writer's block. To overcome this, he turned to his Mac (likely a PowerBook, given it was 1997) and used a program called SimpleText. He wrote various slogans and then employed the computer's speech synthesis function to vocalize them, resulting in the unique, unsettling, and powerful delivery heard on "Fitter Happier." "Tom had run into a bad case of writer's block It was looking for some way to break through so he turned to his Mac This is 1997 so it must have been some kind of power book and a program called simple text Tom just wrote a bunch of slogans into the program and let the computer speak"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Toenail Clippings Sold on eBay – Fan Collected Discarded Clippings from Dressing Room
xref.body: A Radiohead fan managed to collect a quantity of Thom Yorke's toenail clippings, apparently retrieved from a dressing room. The clippings were listed for sale on eBay and sold. This is cited as an example of the extreme lengths some music fans will go to possess physical matter from a performer they idolize. "One Radiohead fan somehow managed to collect a pile of Thom Yorke's toenail clippings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
